Chapter 1: The Foundation—Adopting a Mindset That Anything Can Be Solved.
At the heart of personal growth and real achievement, there’s this one simple idea that changes everything: every problem, no matter how big or intimidating it seems, can be solved.
Now, this isn’t just something you write on a sticky note for motivation. It’s actually a mindset—a lens that completely shifts how you see and deal with challenges.
Think about it like this: what if you treated every locked door in your life as if it has a key? Sure, sometimes it takes a while to find that key, but the important part is that you’re looking for it, not just sitting down and giving up.
Here’s the thing—believing that a solution is possible, even if you don’t know what it is yet, is the very first step toward actually finding it. That belief keeps your energy moving forward, instead of getting stuck in frustration or defeat.
Maybe you’ve seen this play out in real life—a parent who manages to fix things around the house with whatever tools are lying around, or a mentor who always seems to find a creative way through tough situations. People like this show us that resourcefulness isn’t about knowing everything. It’s about not giving up on figuring things out.
If you want to really adopt this way of thinking, it helps to shift from a fixed mindset—where you assume your abilities or circumstances can’t change—to a growth mindset, where you see skills and results as things you can build with effort and learning.
I’ll be honest, making this shift isn’t always easy. It means challenging those old beliefs that whisper things like “this is impossible” or “I just can’t do it.” You’ve got to get comfortable with experimenting, failing sometimes, and then giving it another shot.
One super practical way to start? Try using the phrase “everything is figureoutable” as a mental anchor. The next time you hit a wall, say it to yourself. It might sound simple, but just repeating those words can snap you out of a downward spiral of doubt. Suddenly, you’re opening up space for new ideas and creative problem-solving.
If you make this a habit, over time you’ll notice your automatic response to challenges shifts from helplessness to curiosity—and even determination.
Here’s how you can put this into practice, step by step:
First, recognize those limiting beliefs. When you catch yourself thinking “I can’t do this,” or “this is impossible,” pause for a moment. Those thoughts are just signals, not facts.
Next, try to reframe the challenge. Instead of seeing a roadblock, imagine it’s a puzzle waiting to be solved.
And finally, make a real commitment to finding a way forward—even if it takes longer than you’d like.
Look, this mindset won’t make your obstacles disappear overnight. But it does change your whole relationship with them. Instead of feeling stuck, you’ll start to take action, try new things, and bounce back from setbacks more easily.
When you believe solutions exist, your mind gets better at noticing opportunities, spotting resources, and coming up with creative ideas you might’ve otherwise missed.
This isn’t just theory. People from all walks of life—entrepreneurs launching new businesses, folks changing careers, or anyone facing a personal setback—have used this mindset to move forward. The common thread isn’t some kind of superhuman talent. It’s simply a willingness to believe that with enough effort and some resourcefulness, progress is always possible.
